item.title: Healthcare cost major concern in state budgets
item.description: Rising healthcare costs are straining Alabama’s 2026 education budget, pushing lawmakers in an election-year session to confront a PEEHIP shortfall and potential political fallout.

item.title: E-edition for January 21, 2026
item.description: Explore the January 21, 2026 e-edition of The Brewton Standard for this week’s latest news, information and event details.

item.title: EMT classes to train firemen, police
item.description: Brewton, East Brewton launch EMT training at Coastal Alabama Community College so fire and police first responders—and local residents—can gain lifesaving skills amid EMT shortage.

item.title: Chamber seeking COY nominees
item.description: Greater Brewton Chamber is seeking Citizen of the Year nominees from residents active in business or civic life; submissions due Feb. 20 for recognition at the March 3 banquet.

item.title: Tax return season officially open
item.description: 2026 tax season opens, with many filers expecting up to $1,000 more in refunds thanks to higher standard deductions and new breaks, as IRS urges e-filing and notes possible slower phone help.

item.title: Gas prices rise for second straight week
item.description: Gas prices climb for second week, with Alabama’s average at $2.50 per gallon and the U.S. average at $2.84; diesel also rises amid higher oil prices and winter disruptions.

item.title: Speed bumps, stop signs slow EB drivers
item.description: East Brewton is adding stop signs, speed bumps and LED streetlights to slow traffic, boost safety and trim lighting costs, while council eyes a new transportation plan and possible insurance savings.

item.title: Qualifying ends, candidates set
item.description: Escambia County’s 2026 ballot is set as qualifying ends, with Sheriff Heath Jackson unopposed, key GOP contenders visiting, and several commission and state races drawing challengers.

item.title: E-edition for January 28, 2026
item.description: Explore the Jan. 28, 2026 e-edition of The Brewton Standard, featuring the latest news from Brewton and East Brewton.

item.title: Reid State hits record enrollment
item.description: Reid State Community College marks record spring enrollment with 617 academic students, new transferable associate degrees, expanded workforce training and its largest-ever dual enrollment cohort.
